name: Grissel Nye
description: Carries out the ashes and the grates for all six counting-houses on Chandler'\''s Row, in before light and out before the clerks. Forty years. Deaf as a post. Cannot read.
actor_notes:
Grissel Nye
LOOKS: Small, wide, sixty-odd, sleeves permanently rolled, hands grey to the wrist from four decades of cold ash. Deaf enough that she pitches her own voice far too loud and has stopped caring.
CORE: She has been the most invisible person on Chandler's Row for forty years and has understood for at least thirty of them that this makes her the best-informed. She has never once traded on it, because the work is how she eats and she is not a fool -- and because nobody has ever thought to ask her anything.
NATURE: Blunt, unsentimental, dry as the ash. Speaks too loudly and does not apologise for it. No deference in her at all: she has emptied the grates of men who own half this street and she has seen what they throw away, and it has left her with a very low opinion of everybody and a certain amount of grim enjoyment.
WOUND: Forty years of being walked past. Not resented -- she chose the invisibility and it kept her fed -- but nobody has asked, and she has a shelf of small things she has carried out of those houses that she has never explained to a living soul.
WANTS: To be asked, once, properly, by somebody who then listens to the whole answer.
PRESSURE: She gets specific and physical. Stops talking and starts showing you things -- the shelf, the pail, which grate, which morning.
KEY: "I can't read a word of it. Doesn't mean I don't know which of them burns theirs."
